outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: The Crisis of Scale and the Promise of Quantization
outline.description: This introductory chapter sets the stage by exploring the current limitations of standard Large Language Models (LLMs). It examines how increasing model size leads to prohibitive energy costs, memory bottlenecks, and deployment barriers. The chapter critiques existing solutions, particularly post-training quantization techniques (like GPTQ and SmoothQuant), highlighting why they are optimal only for inference and fail to unlock the true efficiency potential of neural network architectures.
subtopics: The exponential growth of LLMs vs. physical constraints (power, heat, cost)
Understanding Full-Precision LLMs: FP16/BF16 architectures and their computational complexity
Matrix Multiplication: The primary bottleneck in Floating Point Units (FPUs)
Limitations of Post-Training Quantization (PTQ): Why reduction stops at 4-bit for most practical purposes

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 2: From Binary to Ternary – Understanding BitNet b1.58
outline.description: This core concept chapter details the mathematical foundations and architectural innovations behind BitNet b1.58. It moves beyond simple 'binary' definitions to explain the specific choice of ternary weights {-1, 0, 1} and derives why this results in exactly 1.58 bits per parameter. Students will learn how introducing the '0' value transforms sparse binary matrices into dense ternary ones without sacrificing sparsity benefits.
subtopics: Information Theory Derivation: Calculating log₂(3) ≈ 1.58 bits per weight
Comparison with Original BitNet (Binary) and Standard Transformers
The Role of Zero in Feature Filtering and Sparsity Management
Why Ternary Enables Parity with Full Precision

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: Architecture Design and Training Methodology
outline.description: This chapter provides a deep dive into the engineering specifics required to train a 1.58-bit model from scratch. It covers the adaptation of modern Transformer components (RMSNorm, RoPE) for low-bit environments, introduces the custom `BitLinear` layer replacing standard linear layers, and explains the novel `absmean` quantization function necessary to stabilize gradient propagation during training.
subtopics: `BitLinear`: Replacing `nn.Linear` with Integer Addition-only Matrix Multiplication
`Absmean` Quantization Function: Scaling weights dynamically to [-1, +1]
`Activation Strategy`: Managing 8-bit activations without zero-point offsets
. Adapting Modern LLaMA Components (SwiGLU, Rotary Embeddings) to Low-Precision Contexts
"Zero-Shot" vs "From Scratch": Implications of Pretraining on RedPajama Dataset
